---
title: SFT with MS-Swift
---

## Convert trajectories

SearchAgent includes a converter from OpenSeeker-style agent trajectories to the
MS-Swift JSONL format:

```bash
searchagent plugins convert \
  data/openseeker.jsonl \
  outputs/sft/ms_swift.jsonl
```

Use `--max-records` to limit conversion samples.

Inspect several converted rows. Confirm that system, user, assistant, tool-call, and
tool-result messages are ordered correctly and match the model's intended tool format.

## Run SFT training

Install [MS-Swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) in a dedicated training
environment, then install SearchAgent into that environment. Configure
`scripts/sft/sft_training.yaml` with the dataset, base model, output directory, context
length, distributed settings, and reporting backend.

Validate the resolved command first:

```bash
python -m searchagent.training.sft \
  --config scripts/sft/sft_training.yaml \
  --dry-run
```

Start training directly or with the environment-aware wrapper:

```bash
python -m searchagent.training.sft --config scripts/sft/sft_training.yaml
```

```bash
SFT_MODEL=/models/Qwen3-8B \
SFT_TRAIN_DATASET=outputs/sft/ms_swift.jsonl \
SFT_OUTPUT_DIR=outputs/sft/model \
bash scripts/sft/sft_train.sh
```

The launcher builds a `swift sft` command from structured YAML and rejects unknown
fields. Put uncommon MS-Swift flags under `backend.extra_args`.

## Evaluate the trained model

Serve the checkpoint through an API compatible with the selected SearchAgent client,
then run the same inference recipe and dataset used for the baseline:

```bash
searchagent run --config-name webexplorer \
  agent.llm_client.model=/models/searchagent-sft \
  agent.llm_client.openai.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1 \
  dataloader.source=data/eval.jsonl \
  output_path=outputs/sft_eval
```

Evaluate the saved histories with the same answer extractor and judge settings as the
baseline. In addition to final accuracy, compare tool-call validity, repeated searches,
turn count, context usage, and failure rate.
